title: Run the function-signature check locally with --base-revision; the script no longer fetches the base branch
answers: how do I run the function signature check locally
check_function_signatures.py base branch not found locally
how to compare my branch against master for signature breaking changes
what flag sets the base for the signature check
body:
Invoke: `uv run --no-project dev/check_function_signatures.py --base-revision master` (the default is $GITHUB_BASE_REF if set, else `master`).
The script runs `git diff --name-only BASE HEAD` and `git show BASE:path` directly, and no longer runs `git fetch origin BASE:BASE`, so the revision must already exist locally (for example `git fetch origin master:master` first, or a full clone).
Any ref works, e.g. `--base-revision HEAD^1` to compare the last commit, or a release branch name; argument parsing is in dev/check_function_signatures.py:parse_args.
applies: Local invocation of dev/check_function_signatures.py; CI uses HEAD^1 explicitly and does not depend on this default.

search: Running dev/check_function_signatures.py locally using --base-revision to compare signatures against an existing local git ref. The script runs git diff --name-only BASE HEAD and git show BASE:path without fetching from origin, defaulting to $GITHUB_BASE_REF or master. Invocation is uv run --no-project dev/check_function_signatures.py --base-revision master (or any ref such as HEAD^1), whereas CI specifies HEAD^1 explicitly.
